key_insight: This paper shows that in embodied reinforcement learning, privacy leakage can go beyond single-step gradient attacks: temporal structure in policy gradients can reveal entire private trajectories. The proposed TRACE attack reconstructs consecutive observation-action sequences autoregressively from per-step gradients.
problem_solved: It addresses the privacy risk in distributed embodied RL, where raw sensor data stays on-device but policy gradients sent to a server can still expose private temporal behavior and trajectories.
method: Introduces TRACE (Temporal Reconstruction Attack on Consecutive Encodings), an amortized temporal gradient-inversion attack.
Uses autoregressive reconstruction to recover private observation-action trajectories step by step from per-step policy gradients.
Exploits temporal dependencies across consecutive encodings to improve leakage beyond single-frame inversion attacks.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this work highlights that gradient sharing in embodied RL can leak more information than expected, especially when data has strong temporal structure. It underscores the need for stronger privacy defenses when training distributed agents in sensor-rich environments.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing on-device sensing, gradient transmission, and server-side trajectory reconstruction
Timeline visualization of consecutive observation-action steps reconstructed autoregressively
Side-by-side comparison of single-frame attack vs. temporal attack leakage
Icon-based privacy graphic showing private trajectory data exposed through gradients
paper_title: Temporal Gradient Inversion for Private Trajectory Reconstruction in Embodied Reinforcement Learning
paper_authors: Sudip Bhujel, Shanghao Shi, Ruiquan Huang, Ning Zhang, Yang Xiao
